text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
LES ECHOS
-- Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn calls for case-by-case approach to privatisations, adds previous government had made committment to European Commission to privatise insurer GAN.

-- Blue-chip CAC 40 index fell by over two percent yesterday on announcement the government considering raising taxes targetting profitable businesses. Finance Minister Strauss-Kahn said no decision had yet been taken on any budget measures.
-- Guinness and GrandMet agree to consider merging their spirits divisions with that of luxury goods group LVMH.
-- Paribas chairman Andre Levy-Lang says Paribas has the means to carry on with its strategy, does not rule out an acquisition in the investment banking sector.
-- Finance Ministry publishes accounts of CDR company set up to sell off Credit Lyonnais assets, confirms CDR losses of up to a hundred billion francs, plans to re-organise CDR.
LA TRIBUNE
-- Unemployment fund Unedic expects 15,000 to 95,000 more jobseekers in 1997, raised unemployment benefits by 2.2 percent as of July 1.
-- Prime Minister's office does not rule out a privatisatiuon of Thomson-CSF to speed up a restructuring of the French defence industry in a context of European co-operation.
-- Insurer GAN and its banking unit CIC re-negotiate their banking and insurance co-operation agreements.
L'AGEFI
-- European Commission drafts a book outlining technical aspects of a switch of European financial markets to a single currency.
LE FIGARO-ECONOMIE
-- Government seeks new revenues and may increase taxes on businesses' profits. Employers fear it would result in a drop in companies' investments.
-- A 1996 embargo on exports of British beef possibly hit by BSE "mad cow" disease has allegedly been violated, including shipments to France.
LIBERATION (Economic section)
-- Unedic to raise unemployment benefits as of July 1.
THE INTERNATIONAL HERALD TRIBUNE
-- Axa UAP merges British insurance and asset-management units.
